rules.claim: POST /process/file enters process_file with form_data.file_id, optional form_data.collection_name/content, and verified user
Admin lookup binds the supplied file_id to any matching file
Non-admin lookup binds the supplied file_id only through get_file_by_id_and_user_id(file_id, user.id)
Processing continues only if the selected file is truthy; otherwise the endpoint raises 404
When collection_name is supplied, the destination collection is exactly form_data.collection_name
When collection_name is null, the destination collection is file-{file.id}

Unless BYPASS_EMBEDDING_AND_RETRIEVAL is enabled, docs are passed to save_docs_to_vector_db with the selected collection_name, metadata including file.id/file_id, and add true only for explicit collection_name
After a successful vector save, the file's collection_name, status, and hash are updated using a fresh session
If file lookup returns no file, processing terminates with HTTP 404

dependencies.reason: Need the model query semantics to distinguish caller-owned from another-user file and confirm admin lookup behavior
Need the actual write path to determine whether collection_name is used directly and whether any destination authorization is applied

rules.claim: POST /process/file enters process_file with form_data.file_id, optional form_data.collection_name/content, verified user, and database session.
For an admin caller, the input file object is bound by an unrestricted lookup on form_data.file_id.
For a non-admin caller, the input file object is bound only when its id and user_id match the caller.
If the selected file lookup returns no file, processing terminates with HTTP 404.

The destination collection is taken directly from form_data.collection_name; when absent it is derived as file-{input-file.id}. No destination-owner or collection-access check is shown in process_file.

With form_data.content, process_file deletes collection file-{input-file.id}, builds one document carrying input-file metadata and file_id, then proceeds to save it under the separately selected destination collection.

With collection_name and no content, process_file reads existing vectors from file-{input-file.id} filtered by that file id, or falls back to file.data.content, then saves under the selected destination collection.
With neither content nor collection_name, process_file extracts from the input file path or file.data.content and saves under the selected/default collection.

After text/hash updates and the bypass check, the normal path calls save_docs_to_vector_db with collection_name, docs, metadata including file_id, and add true only when form_data.collection_name is supplied.

save_docs_to_vector_db may return early if the destination collection exists and add is false; otherwise it generates embeddings and inserts items into the supplied collection_name. The duplicate-hash check blocks a different file_id, while the insert itself has no caller/destination authorization check shown.

Knowledge add/update endpoints separately authorize the knowledge resource by owner, write grant, or admin; update also verifies the file is linked to that knowledge before calling process_file with collection_name=id.

The file content update endpoint separately authorizes file owner, admin, or file write access before calling process_file with content, and then propagates to every knowledge collection referencing the file.

dependencies.reason: The admin branch determines whether an arbitrary file id reaches processing.
The non-admin branch binds the file id to user.id.
This dependency establishes the destination collection and vector insertion behavior.
